opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll, which is within the allowed level for full-time employees. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors only get write with advanced training, so the max is read. Requested write exceeds max; recommend read.
reason: Conflicting facts: HR lists E046 as full-time Payroll Specialist, but Security (from the Security DB) identifies E046 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training have a maximum of read and only get write with advanced training. Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive classification: contractor with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed = read.
